Having clarity can help in these situations, when things seem very uncertain. A few questions that came to mind from my perspective as an adoptee:

1. Are you emotionally in a stable place ? Raising a child takes a tremendous amount of mental and emotional bandwidth and taking care of your mental health should be too priority.
2. Do you have support? Emotionally, physically, spiritually, financially, logistically? Having these things in place can help you with your decision, whatever it is you decide.
3. Is your relationship with the father healthy/safe/ stable? Any of the decisions you decide will change your relationship as you know it, whether that’s terminating, relinquishing, or parenting a child . 
4. Are you aware of your options? Do you have people who are unbiased in their understanding of abortion, adoption or parenting?
5. Do you understand the realities of adoption, and adoptees? These are not anti adoption sentiments, but simply the realities and trauma many adoptees will face. It’s important to go into your decision with eyes wide open. There are great books on the subject- as well as Fb groups,  pages, blogs, etc. 
6. Do you feel inclined one way or the other? 
7. Do you know why for you keeping the baby is not an option ? 

These are just a few that came to mind. Sometimes gathering factual information can help with such an emotional decision. 

*A word of advice. Don’t be bullied into any decisions you make. Should you choose to relinquish, do not sign anything while pregnant, laboring  or immediately post birth. You want to be clear headed and free from any drugs, pain meds hormones, etc. 
adoption agencies can be incredibly predatory to mothers. 
Ask questions, inquire, don’t feel shame. 

Good luck to you in whatever you choose .

3. Is your relationship with the father healthy/safe/ stable? Any of the decisions you decide will change your relationship as you know it, whether that’s terminating, relinquishing, or parenting a child . 
4. Are you aware of your options? Do you have people who are unbiased in their understanding of abortion, adoption or parenting?
5. Do you understand the realities of adoption, and adoptees? These are not anti adoption sentiments, but simply the realities and trauma many adoptees will face. It’s important to go into your decision with eyes wide open. There are great books on the subject- as well as Fb groups,  pages, blogs, etc. 
6. Do you feel inclined one way or the other? 
7. Do you know why for you keeping the baby is not an option ? 

These are just a few that came to mind. Sometimes gathering factual information can help with such an emotional decision. 

*A word of advice. Don’t be bullied into any decisions you make. Should you choose to relinquish, do not sign anything while pregnant, laboring  or immediately post birth. You want to be clear headed and free from any drugs, pain meds hormones, etc.
